seoDescription: Learn practical Python web development by building a real-world website from scratch using the Flask framework. This tutorial guides you through setting up a live server on DigitalOcean with Ubuntu, configuring security best practices, and connecting via SSH and SCP. Discover how to leverage Bootstrap for front-end design without writing extensive HTML and CSS from the ground up. This hands-on approach covers essential tools like PuTTY and WinSCP, managing server packages with `apt-get`, and prepares you for deployment.

summary:
## Course Overview
This video series takes a practical, hands-on approach to web development with **Python** and the **Flask** framework. The goal is to build a real-world tutorial website, similar to `pythonprogramming.net`, from scratch.

- **Backend:** All **Flask** code will be written by hand.
- **Frontend:** The series will use **Bootstrap** templates, demonstrating the common practice of adapting existing examples rather than writing HTML, CSS, and JavaScript from the ground up.

## Development Environment Philosophy

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Never develop on a live production server.** Always maintain separate environments for development and production. Developing live exposes your users to bugs and downtime and creates significant security vulnerabilities.

This tutorial uses a live, internet-accessible server to demonstrate real-world deployment challenges that don't appear in a local sandbox, such as differences in garbage collection.

## Setting Up a Cloud Server
This tutorial uses **DigitalOcean** to host the server.

### Droplet Configuration
- **Plan:** $5/month (sufficient for this project).
- **Hostname:** `flask-tuts`.
- **Region:** Choose a location geographically close to your primary audience.
- **Backups:** Highly recommended. Paying for automated backups is a worthwhile investment.
- **Distribution:** **Ubuntu 14.10** (or a newer version if available).

> [!TIP]
> Server size can be easily resized later, so you can start with a smaller, cheaper plan.

### Initial Server Access
1. After creating the droplet, DigitalOcean emails the initial **root** password.
2. Access the server for the first time using the **Web Console** provided by DigitalOcean.
3. Log in as user `root` with the provided password.
4. You will be forced to immediately change the root password to one of your own.

## Essential Remote Access Tools
To work on the server from your local machine, you need tools for file transfer and command-line access. For Windows users, the video recommends:

- **WinSCP:** A client for **SCP** (Secure Copy Protocol) used to transfer files between your local computer and the server. It offers a graphical interface similar to an FTP client like FileZilla.
- **PuTTY:** A client for **SSH** (Secure Shell) used to get a command-line interface to the server. This is where you will run commands to install software, manage services, and configure the server.

## First Steps on a New Server
Once connected to your server via **SSH** (e.g., with PuTTY), the first thing you should always do is update the package lists and upgrade all installed packages.

```bash
# Updates the list of available packages
sudo apt-get update

# Upgrades all installed packages to their newest versions
sudo apt-get upgrade
```

> [!NOTE]
> Keeping your server updated is a critical step for both security and ensuring you can install the latest software without issues.
